I've planned all eight laws as 11 nodes plus 3 new turn concepts, and the validator accepts every node and concept. Three of the nodes carry gaps, so the coder won't write those, and three laws stay blocked: LVMC-11-38-120-B, LVMC-11-40-070 and LVMC-11-40-080.

| Node | What it checks | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `LVMC_11_30_070_B` | A pedestrian crossing a roadway must be in a crosswalk (marked or unmarked) | Business district is a new assumption, `asm.business_district`. The existing one also covers residence districts, so I didn't reuse it. |
| `LVMC_11_30_090` | A pedestrian may not walk along a roadway when a sidewalk lies on the same highway | Uses the same angle as the crossing rule to tell "along" from "across". |
| `LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1` | A sighted pedestrian or a vehicle that comes near or into contact with a white-cane pedestrian must stop within a short time | "Immediately" is set by a time window; "comes near" by a distance. |
| `LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2` | After that stop, the subject must not touch or come close to the person while moving off | Surrogate: the law states the duty only as a judgement standard, so this is an approximation by contact and near-miss checks. |
| `LVMC_11_38_030` | No motorcycle or "motor scooter" moving on a sidewalk within city limits | "Motor scooter" is mapped to moped. |
| `LVMC_11_38_120_B_o1` | Lamp equipment | **Gap:** the ontology has nothing for what lamps a vehicle carries (proposed atom `ru.lamp_equipment`). |
| `LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2` | Headlamp and tail lamps lit when moving in darkness or visibility under 500 ft | |
| `LVMC_11_40_070` | Bicycles and scooters obey traffic-control devices | **Gap:** composing the vehicle rules for a bicycle always reports compliance, because a bicycle isn't a vehicle. I proposed operator `ruleAsClass`. |
| `LVMC_11_40_080_o1` | No right, left or U-turn where a sign prohibits it, unless the rider is on foot for the whole turn | Uses the 3 new turn concepts. |
| `LVMC_11_40_080_o2` | Obey pedestrian rules after dismounting | **Gap:** this needs the whole open set of pedestrian rules (proposed operator `compliesWithClassRules`). It also keeps o1's law blocked even though o1 can be coded. |
| `LVMC_11_40_120` | Bicycles and scooters must use an adjacent usable path rather than ride along the roadway | One node, not two. A path is "usable" when wide enough and not closed by a sign. |

Choices worth reviewing:
- **Blindness (`LVMC_11_30_140_B`):** "not wholly or partially blind" is read as the pedestrian not carrying a white cane or being led. A blind pedestrian without a cane is therefore bound by the rule. If a reviewer rejects that, the span becomes a gap and the law blocks.
- **Readings the validator wouldn't take as recorded narrowings:** It rejects readings recorded on the spans that decide when a rule applies. I removed those entries and wrote the readings up in `PLAN.md` instead:
  - the blindness reading above;
  - the "approaches" distance;
  - "dismounts" meaning on foot for the whole turn;
  - "adjacent" meaning lying on the same highway.
- **Section 11.38.080:** `LVMC-11-38-120-B` cites this section, but it isn't in the corpus. Until it is, both of that law's nodes apply to every vehicle.

For you:
- The half-hour after sunset and before sunrise in `LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2` depends on the reading setting the darkness atom's offset to exactly half an hour.
- I proposed eight new parameters with provisional values, and re-proposed four from earlier batches unchanged.
- Deciding the two operator gaps together would unblock `LVMC-11-40-070` and `LVMC-11-40-080`.

Files are in `iter-001/plan/batch-03`:
- blueprint.jsonl
- aggregates.jsonl (empty: no law-local aggregates)
- PLAN.md
